I've been farming these 6 mu for 30 years, since I was 16. My old man taught me, and now my wife and our two kids help when they're not busy. We don't have much land, so every mu has to pull its weight. I only finished primary school, so I don't know all those formulas the extension people talk about. I watch what my neighbors do, remember what happened on my own fields, and try not to spend more than I have in my pocket.

**Winter wheat — 5 mu**

It's early October now, and I need to get the wheat in the ground soon. I plant around the same time every year, usually right after National Day. Last year I got about 360 kg per mu from this plot, which was okay — not great, but not a disaster either. My neighbor Lao Zhang uses a bit more fertilizer than me and gets closer to 400, but he has a son working in the factory sending money home. I don't have that luxury, so I have to be careful.

I saved most of my seed from last year, but I bought a small bag of new seed to mix in — about 35 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I do what I always do: one bag of compound fertilizer spread before planting, that's my base. Then in March, if the wheat looks yellow after winter, I topdress with urea at jointing. I figure about 14 kg of nitrogen per mu total, maybe a little phosphorus from the compound bag. I don't usually bother with extra potassium — the compound fertilizer has some, and that's enough for me.

I'll irrigate three times: once right after planting to help it germinate, once in spring when it wakes up, and once at grain filling if it doesn't rain. Pumping water costs money, about 25 yuan each time per mu, so three times is already pushing it. But wheat is my food security — if the wheat fails, my family doesn't have enough flour for the year. So I spend on water here.

For pests, I'll spray herbicide once in early spring. The weeds get bad if I don't. I plow the field once after the maize comes off, then rotary tillage, broadcast the seed, and roll it. My family does all the work — planting takes about 10 days of family labor, and another few days for fertilizing and spraying. No hired labor for wheat, I can't afford it.

**Summer maize — 5 mu (same land, after wheat)**

This is the tricky part. When wheat comes off in early June, I have maybe a week to get the maize in. Last year I was slow and planted late, and the yield suffered. This year I'll hire the planter from the village — costs me about one day's wage, but he gets it done fast and straight. The seed is hybrid, about 45 yuan per mu. I always use hybrid for maize — saved seed doesn't work, everyone knows that.

I put all the fertilizer down at planting — one shot of compound fertilizer, about 13 kg nitrogen worth. I don't split it for maize, there's no time and anyway the summer rains usually wash some in. I irrigate twice if it's dry — once right after planting, once at tasseling. If the summer rains are good, maybe only once. 

Weeds are bad in maize too, so herbicide. And last year there were armyworms in the village, so I'll keep an eye out and maybe spray insecticide if I see them. I don't do it preventively — that costs too much. Direct seeding into the wheat stubble, no tillage, no time for tillage. Family handles the harvest and drying, about 8 days total. One day hired for planting.

**Stevia — 1 mu**

I started this two years ago after my cousin said the buyer in the county pays good money for it. It's only 1 mu, on the corner near the well. I don't dare do more — if the price drops, I still need my wheat and maize to eat. I plant seedlings in late April, after the wheat is already established but before maize. Harvest is multiple picks from July through October.

Stevia needs more hand work — weeding, picking, drying. That's why it's only 1 mu. My wife and I do all the labor, about 25 family days over the season. I fertilize it light — two times, base and after first cut, about 8 kg nitrogen total. Irrigate twice, same well. I spray herbicide and insecticide because the leaves have to be clean or the buyer rejects them. I hope to get about 120 kg of dried leaves per mu, but honestly it varies a lot.

**Why I'm doing it this way**

Money is tight. My total cash for inputs this season is about 2,200 yuan, and that's already most of what I saved from last year. I thought about putting more fertilizer on the wheat like Lao Zhang, but if I spend that money and then the spring is dry, I'm worse off. Better to spend a little less and have cash left if my daughter needs school fees or someone gets sick. The stevia is my gamble — if it pays off, I have extra income. If not, I still have my 5 mu of grain to fall back on. That's how I survive — don't put all your eggs in one basket, and always keep some cash under the mattress.
